rounds.text: Gujarat Credit Corporation Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at a steep discount with a price-to-book ratio of just 0.51x against a book value of 38.5 rupees per share [E2]. This asset discount is reinforced by a compelling discounted cash flow model indicating an intrinsic value of 33 rupees per share, offering a substantial 40.5% margin of safety [E35, E36]. Furthermore, the market price currently bakes in a modest 9.5% earnings growth expectation via the reverse DCF, which contrasts sharply with the actual accelerating growth profile demonstrated by a trailing twelve-month profit expansion of 279% and a 5-year compounded profit growth of 19% [E14, E16, E37, E49]. Insider conviction is also aligning with this value proposition, as promoters have actively increased their stake to 33.44% by late 2026 from 31.61% in late 2023 [E33]. Conceded: the debt-to-equity ratio sits at 1.68x alongside low multi-year returns on equity [E21, E29]. Yet, current operating momentum signals a powerful turnaround, with results scoring 81 out of 100 on the back of a 78% year-over-year net profit surge that stale sentiment fails to price in [E46, E51].

Gujarat Credit Corporation Ltd carries severe structural and financial risks that undermine its low price-to-book ratio [E2, E7]. The company exhibits atrocious profitability metrics, highlighted by a multi-year median return on equity stuck at 1% or lower across 10-year, 5-year, and 1-year horizons, and dropping to -2% over the last 3 years [E20, E21, E22, E23, E43]. Balance sheet distress is glaring: the current ratio sits at an alarming 0.15x as current liabilities heavily eclipse current assets, while leverage is elevated with a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.68x and total borrowings expanding to Rs 19.47 Cr [E29, E30, E31]. Cash generation has completely collapsed, producing a negative operating cash flow of Rs -5.00 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -6.24 Cr for Mar 2026, leading to a dreadful cash conversion ratio of -62.50x [E26, E27, E28]. Furthermore, valuation metrics relative to peers and earnings are heavily inflated, with an EV/EBITDA of 811.3x against a sector benchmark of 13.11x and a P/E reaching 78.71x compared to the sector benchmark of 18.76x [E6, E11]. Compounded share price performance reflects this fundamental weakness, dropping by 23% over the past year and sitting merely 6% above its 52-week low [E5, E19]. Conceded: the company demonstrates short-term profit acceleration with compounded profit growth reaching 279% in the trailing twelve months and a discounted cash flow valuation sitting above the current market price [E16, E35, E46].

Conceded: multi-year median return on equity is low at 1% or lower across historical horizons, and current liabilities exceed current assets [E20, E22, E30]. However, dismissing the business on these stagnant historical ratios ignores a powerful ongoing turnaround where trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth has surged by 279% alongside a 78% year-over-year jump in net profit [E16, E46, E51]. The market price of Rs 19.8 is severely disconnected from the company's true worth, sitting at a steep discount to a book value of Rs 38.5 and offering a price-to-book ratio of just 0.51x [E2]. This mispricing provides a substantial margin of safety of 40.5% based on discounted cash flow intrinsic value, while a reverse DCF demonstrates that the current price merely prices in a modest 9.5% earnings growth rate [E35, E36, E37]. Furthermore, insiders are actively backing this trajectory, with promoter holding increasing by 1.83 percentage points to 33.44% [E33]. Finally, the current price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range while results score an impressive 81 out of 100, proving that stale sentiment is masking an accelerating earnings recovery [E5, E51].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth surged by 279% [E16], net profit jumped 78% year-over-year [E46], and promoters increased holdings by 1.83 percentage points to 33.44% [E33]. However, citing these short-term metrics ignores severe, structural balance sheet distress that makes the low price-to-book ratio of 0.51x a value trap rather than a margin of safety [E2]. The current liabilities overwhelmingly exceed current assets with a disastrous current ratio of 0.15x, and borrowings have expanded to Rs 19.47 Cr, leaving debt exceeding net worth at a leverage risk of 1.68x [E29, E30, E31]. Furthermore, cash generation has completely collapsed as operating cash flow turned negative to Rs -5.00 Cr alongside a staggering cash conversion of -62.50x, culminating in a free cash outflow of Rs -6.24 Cr [E26, E27, E28]. This alarming cash burn is compounded by a flagged risk that the company might be capitalizing its interest costs, rendering reported profit growth highly suspect [E44]. Finally, valuation metrics like the EV/EBITDA of 811.3x and a P/E of 78.71x against sector benchmarks prove that the underlying operational reality is wildly overvalued relative to peers, regardless of where the stock sits in its 52-week range [E5, E6, E11].
